note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a CIV 24-33, 39-41; A06b CIV 24-33, 39-41; L05 CIV 48): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Wedlock restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. The coding also records a wedlock restriction (a child born out of wedlock may not take it from a citizen father), which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Cote dIvoire, 2024
sources.said: Person has been habitually and legally resident in Cote d'Ivoire for 5 years. ... n.a. ... Person acquires citizenship of another country.  Loss is subordinated to authorisation of government during 15 period following inscription on lists for military service (these lists were never established). ... Wedlock restriction ... Person is born in Cote d'Ivoire in wedlock or descent to a citizen is established (unless descent is established to one or both parents who are foreigners). ... Generally applicable provision ... Person born abroad to a citizen in wedlock, or out of wedlock and descent is established to a parent who is a citizen. ... No provision ... No provision
